attrs.evidence: spec_release.mjs v0.2.0: RELEASE_FIELD_PLANES over 15 fields, an unclassified field is a failure, DERIVED fields are recomputed and compared, release_type and all three protocol identifiers are CHECKED against docs/spec/proof-wire/schema/, and the vector count is derived from the input directory. Gate `gov-nest`. The forged-manifest attack now draws seven named disagreements.
attrs.statement: EVERY AUTHORITATIVE FIELD OF A RELEASE MANIFEST IS DERIVED, CHECKED, DECLARED_AND_BOUND, OR EXPLICITLY NON_AUTHORITATIVE, and there is no fifth category. A release verifier that checks component digests while letting the release record declare what those digests MEAN is B6.3 at the release layer: measured, a manifest whose release_type, protocol identifiers, both revision labels, upstream repository, vector count and holdout count were all forged -- with every component digest left honest -- PASSED, and the verifier PRINTED the forged revision, the forged vector count and the forged holdout count while reporting the release valid. Counts are DERIVED and not arithmetic on a directory listing: `files.length / 2` reported 3.5 upstream vectors because a provenance document made the file count odd, which is harmless and is a perfect small witness that release metadata must be computed rather than estimated. Protocol identifiers are CHECKED against the normative machine-readable schema, which is itself inside the digest the release binds, so a release cannot rename a protocol.
